why: Rule 7/2: zoom shows 18001 as the upstream apex of a V whose two prongs both open toward +z with nothing of the event at lower z, and the shower core sits 20-50 cm downstream of it.
Rule 1 at a junction: 10002 is the apex of a 61 deg two-prong, the 12.2 cm prong Braggs at 10000 (375k tip) and the 5.6 cm proton rises to 200k toward 10003, so both point away.
Rule 7: every dQ/dx reading is flat, but 16001 is the MIP-blue base of the 48 cm cluster-16 chain that warms to 100-120k as it climbs in +y/+z, i.e. the shower apex, and it is the low-z corner.
Rule 1 on a lone 11 cm proton: p4 falls monotonically from 230k at 13000 to 50k at 13002, so 13002 is the start; it is also the lower-z end, but there is no junction to corroborate it.
Rule 1 at a junction: 7002 joins a 57.7 cm MIP muon and a pi+ that Braggs at 7003 (165k); the rival 7000 scores 2-of-2 only on 8037/3077 e/cm readings with its prongs 25 deg apart, a faded track end.
Two-Bragg-ends trap: prong A tips to 128k exactly at 9001 and prong B leaves 9002 as a 40k MIP through 9003 into cluster 44, which peaks 152k at 44016, so 9002 is the junction both point away from.
Rule 7/2: 18001 is the upstream tip of a spray that fans forward to z=490; 18010 next to it is a 167 deg collinear kink, and rule 1's best junction 18008 has 30 cm of event upstream of it.

Rule 3 rules out 8001: seg 8004 rises monotonically 62k-108k over its last 5 cm there and a 9.1 cm e prong hangs off that stop, a Michel; 71057 is left as the lowest-z apex of cluster 71's forward fan whose proton Braggs away at 71063.

Nearly empty event: the only track is a straight 19.5 cm segment whose hot 104k tip is at 22000, making 22001 the start and the lower-z end, but nothing here settles whether the vertex is on this cluster at all.
Same sparse picture: one 18.3 cm single-segment track with a 96k tip at the 22000 end and MIP elsewhere, so 22001 is its start and lowest-z end, but the event has no junction anywhere to confirm it.
Rule 1 at a three-prong junction: a proton rising monotonically to 245k at 12001, a 33 cm MIP muon exiting at the corner, and a faint third prong all radiate from 12003 in the zoom.
Rule 1 plus rule 3: the single 29.5 cm track falls from a 128k Bragg at 11000 to 55k, and a sub-cm blob 4 cm off 11000 marks that as the stopping end, so the start 11001 is the vertex end.

Two Bragg ends (230k at 17001, 208k at 17000) need a common origin, and only 17003 makes both residual-range profiles fall monotonically; it is the dQ/dx minimum and deg 4, but its long prongs are 176 deg apart.
Rule 8: the whole event is one straight 380 cm MIP track at constant z crossing from the y- wall to the x+ wall, flat 40-60k with no Bragg and no junction anywhere, so any click would be invented.
